Every principle the studies use is a rule file under `rules/`: one claim, its
source (a classical text with chapter and verse, a named practitioner's dated
statement, or a published study), its conditions in a machine-readable form,
and reference cases that say when it must fire and when it must stay silent.
This page is generated from those files; nothing here is written by hand.

::: {.af-howto}
**How to read this.** Filter by domain, tier, status or kind of source, or
search by name. The chart counts the rules that match, by domain and tier.
Pick a rule in the table to open its detail: the claim, the conditions
rendered in plain words (rendered, not evaluated), the source with a link, and
each reference case with its outcome when the engine ran it. A rule marked
"needs predicates" is recorded as stated but cannot yet be tested, because the
vocabulary lacks a condition it needs; "needs verification" means its cases
have not been checked against an independent program yet. Classical rules
must cite a text and chapter; rules stated by today's practitioners are
labelled experimental and sit beside them.
:::

```{ojs}
rulesData = FileAttachment("data/rules.json").json()
allRules = rulesData.rules
uniq = (k) => [...new Set(allRules.map((r) => r[k]))].sort()
```

::: {.af-filters}

```{ojs}
viewof domains = Inputs.checkbox(uniq("domain"), { label: "Domain", value: uniq("domain") })
```

```{ojs}
viewof tiers = Inputs.checkbox(uniq("tier"), { label: "Tier", value: uniq("tier") })
```

```{ojs}
viewof statuses = Inputs.checkbox(uniq("status"), { label: "Status", value: uniq("status"),
  format: (s) => s.replace("_", " ") })
```

```{ojs}
viewof sourceTypes = Inputs.checkbox(uniq("source_type"), { label: "Source", value: uniq("source_type") })
```

```{ojs}
viewof query = Inputs.search(allRules, { placeholder: "Search rules", columns: ["id", "name", "claim", "source"] })
```

```{ojs}
viewof chart = Inputs.radio(["By domain", "By source"], { label: "Chart", value: "By domain" })
```

:::

```{ojs}
shown = query.filter((r) => domains.includes(r.domain) && tiers.includes(r.tier)
  && statuses.includes(r.status) && sourceTypes.includes(r.source_type))
tierColor = (t) => (t === "classical" ? palette.series[0] : palette.series[1])
```

```{ojs}
countChart = {
  const key = chart === "By domain" ? "domain" : "source_type";
  const counts = d3.rollups(shown, (v) => v.length, (r) => r[key], (r) => r.tier)
    .flatMap(([k, v]) => v.map(([tier, n]) => ({ k, tier, n })));
  const order = d3.groupSort(shown, (v) => -v.length, (r) => r[key]);
  const plot = Plot.plot({
    width: Math.max(340, Math.min(width, 900)), height: 50 + 34 * Math.max(1, order.length), marginLeft: 150, style: plotStyle,
    x: { label: "Rules", grid: true }, y: { domain: order, label: null },
    color: { type: "identity" },
    marks: [
      Plot.barX(counts, Plot.stackX({ x: "n", y: "k", fill: (d) => tierColor(d.tier), order: ["classical", "experimental"],
        insetRight: 1, insetLeft: 1, title: (d) => `${d.k}, ${d.tier}: ${d.n}`, tip: true })),
      Plot.text(d3.rollups(shown, (v) => v.length, (r) => r[key]), { x: (d) => d[1], y: (d) => d[0], text: (d) => d[1], dx: 8, textAnchor: "start", fill: palette.ink }),
      Plot.ruleX([0], { stroke: palette.axis })
    ]
  });
  return htl.html`<div class="af-chart" id="principles-chart">${plot}</div>`;
}
```

```{ojs}
swatchLegend([{ color: palette.series[0], label: "Classical" }, { color: palette.series[1], label: "Experimental" }])
```

```{ojs}
viewof picked = Inputs.table(shown, {
  columns: ["name", "domain", "tier", "status", "source_type", "source", "reference"],
  header: { name: "Rule", source_type: "Source kind", reference: "Reference cases" },
  format: { status: (s) => s.replace("_", " "), source: (s) => (s.length > 60 ? s.slice(0, 57) + "..." : s) },
  multiple: false, required: false, rows: 14, value: shown[0]
})
```

```{ojs}
function renderTree(node) {
  const kids = node.children && node.children.length
    ? htl.html`<ul class="af-tree">${node.children.map((c) => renderTree(c))}</ul>` : "";
  return htl.html`<li>${node.text}${node.gloss ? htl.html`<div class="af-gloss">${node.gloss}</div>` : ""}${kids}</li>`;
}
REPO = "https://github.com/astro-fusion/astro_research-white-paper/blob/main/"
drawer = {
  const r = picked || shown[0];
  if (!r) return htl.html`<p class="af-notice">No rule matches these filters.</p>`;
  return htl.html`<div class="af-drawer" id="principles-drawer">
    <h3>${r.name}</h3>
    <p><code>${r.id}</code> · ${r.domain} · ${r.tier} · ${r.status.replace("_", " ")} ·
      <a href=${REPO + r.path}>YAML file</a></p>
    <p>${r.claim}</p>
    <h4>Source</h4>
    <p>${r.source_url ? htl.html`<a href=${r.source_url}>${r.source}</a>` : r.source}
      ${r.source_note ? htl.html`<br><span class="af-gloss">${r.source_note}</span>` : ""}</p>
    <h4>Conditions, in plain words</h4>
    ${r.conditions ? htl.html`<ul class="af-tree">${renderTree(r.conditions)}</ul>`
      : htl.html`<p class="af-notice">No machine conditions yet (needs predicates).
        ${r.original_condition.length ? htl.html`As stated: ${r.original_condition.join("; ")}.` : ""}
        ${r.missing_predicates.length ? htl.html`<br>Missing: ${r.missing_predicates.join("; ")}.` : ""}</p>`}
    ${r.window ? htl.html`<p>Window: ${r.window.before ?? 0} ${r.window.unit} before to ${r.window.after ?? 0} ${r.window.unit} after${r.window.note ? ` (${r.window.note})` : ""}.</p>` : ""}
    ${r.expected_effect ? htl.html`<p>Expected effect: ${Object.entries(r.expected_effect).map(([k, v]) => `${k} ${String(v).replace(/\.$/, "")}`).join(", ")}.</p>` : ""}
    <h4>Reference cases</h4>
    ${r.cases.length ? htl.html`<table class="table af-table"><thead><tr><th>Moment</th><th>Expect</th><th>Outcome</th><th>Note</th></tr></thead>
      <tbody>${r.cases.map((c) => htl.html`<tr><td>${c.moment}</td><td>${c.expect}</td>
        <td>${c.outcome}</td><td>${c.note}${c.verified_with ? htl.html`<br><span class="af-gloss">${c.verified_with}</span>` : ""}</td></tr>`)}</tbody></table>`
      : htl.html`<p class="af-notice">No reference cases yet.</p>`}
  </div>`;
}
```

```{ojs}
htl.html`<p class="af-caption">${shown.length} of ${allRules.length} rules shown.
  ${allRules.filter((r) => r.reference.endsWith("pass") && !r.reference.startsWith("0/")).length} rules have reference cases that
  the engine ran; ${allRules.filter((r) => r.status === "needs_predicates").length} need predicates before they can be tested.</p>`
```

To propose a principle for testing, see [Contribute](contribute.qmd).

## Where the rules come from

Each rule names its root: a classical text with chapter and verse and the
translation used, a named practitioner's dated post, video or article, or a
published study. Rules stated by today's practitioners sit beside the
classical ones, labelled experimental, so the field's living practice can be
tested as openly as its texts, and where practitioners disagree both sides are
kept. The policy, the list of sources and the claims still waiting for a
traceable source are in
[Sources of rule development](https://github.com/astro-fusion/astro_research-white-paper/blob/main/docs/research/SOURCES_OF_RULE_DEVELOPMENT.md).

```{ojs}
provenance(rulesData._meta, {
  twin: [],
  note: "the rules table has no paper figure; the same table prints with astro-rules list and astro-rules test"
})
```
